classification.difficultyReason: Express three ground distances through one height, use collinearity to relate adjacent ground angles, and eliminate the shared angular term from two cosine-rule equations.

content.prompt:
An observer from point $A$ sees the top of a pole with an angle of elevation $30^\circ$. After walking $5\text{ m}$ the angle of elevation is now $45^\circ$. After another $8\text{ m}$, the angle of elevation is $60^\circ$.

Find the height of the pole, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Pole OH with three sight lines, collinear route C–B–A, successive distances 8 m and 5 m, and elevation angles 60°, 45° and 30°.
spec.mathematics: C, B and A are collinear in that order; CB:BA=8:5. OH is perpendicular to the horizontal ground plane. HC, HB and HA are solid sight lines; OC, OB, OA and OH retain the source dashed construction style. Screen coordinates describe an illustrative projection, not additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels are supplied givens; no calculated height is visible.

inlines.text: Express the ground distances using tangent, then eliminate the supplementary ground angles with the cosine rule.

answer.worked:
Let $OH=h$ metres and $\theta=\angle OBC$. From the three right-angled triangles,
$$\begin{align*}OA&=\frac{h}{\tan30^\circ}=\sqrt3h\\OB&=\frac{h}{\tan45^\circ}=h\\OC&=\frac{h}{\tan60^\circ}=\frac{h}{\sqrt3}.\end{align*}$$
Since $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear, $\angle OBA=180^\circ-\theta$. Apply the cosine rule in $\triangle OBA$:
$$\begin{align*}OA^2&=OB^2+BA^2-2(OB)(BA)\cos(180^\circ-\theta)\\3h^2&=h^2+25+10h\cos\theta\\10h\cos\theta&=2h^2-25.\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle OBC$:
$$\begin{align*}OC^2&=OB^2+BC^2-2(OB)(BC)\cos\theta\\\frac{h^2}{3}&=h^2+64-16h\cos\theta\\16h\cos\theta&=\frac{2h^2}{3}+64.\end{align*}$$
Eliminate $h\cos\theta$:
$$\begin{align*}16(2h^2-25)&=10\left(\frac{2h^2}{3}+64\right)\\\frac{76h^2}{3}&=1040\\h^2&=\frac{780}{19}\\h&=\sqrt{\frac{780}{19}}\text{ m}\\h&\approx6.4\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
